bias.def: A sampling method is biased if it systematically overestimates or underestimates the population value, in the same direction sample after sample.

voluntary-response.def: A voluntary response sample is made of people who choose themselves, for example by answering an online poll. It overrepresents people with strong opinions.

convenience.def: A convenience sample is made of individuals who are easy to reach, such as shoppers at one store. It is not random and is usually biased.

undercoverage.def: Undercoverage happens when part of the population is left out of the sampling frame, so those individuals have no chance of being chosen.

nonresponse.def: Nonresponse happens when individuals chosen for a sample cannot be reached or do not respond. If they differ from those who respond, the results are biased.

response-bias.def: Response bias happens when answers do not reflect the truth, because of leading question wording, sensitive questions, or pressure from the interviewer or the setting.
